themes_detail.label: Cannabis Retailer Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Cannabis retailer complaints exploded to 5 this week, up 3900% from a 0.1-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74), signaling either rapid illicit dispensary proliferation or a sudden enforcement/community reporting wave in Borough Park/Kensington.
evidence: 5 cannabis retailer complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
3900% spike represents the single largest relative increase across all complaint categories in district
reporting_angles: Ground-level canvass: Are illegal/unlicensed cannabis shops opening on major commercial strips (13th Ave, Coney Island Ave)? Interview residents and shop owners.
Enforcement angle: Has NYPD's Cannabis Enforcement Unit increased patrols or citations this week? Did SLA issue new violations?
Community concern: Speak to local parents, seniors, and business owners about perceived illicit retail activity and quality-of-life impacts.

themes_detail.label: Street Signs Vanishing at 8x Rate
themes_detail.summary: Street sign complaints spiked to 8 this week, up 814% from a 0.9-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 9.13), suggesting coordinated theft, vandalism, or deterioration of wayfinding infrastructure across the district.
evidence: 8 street sign complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.9 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
814% increase indicates pattern, not random fluctuation
reporting_angles: DOT data request: Which intersections/blocks are missing the most signs? Map the pattern to identify hotspots.
Theft or neglect?: Talk to DOT about maintenance backlog vs. reports of targeted sign theft for scrap metal or other value.
Pedestrian safety: Interview community members about navigation difficulty, especially for seniors and non-English speakers relying on street names.

themes_detail.label: Elevator Breakdowns Up 243%
themes_detail.summary: Elevator complaints jumped to 15 last week, up 243% from a 4.4-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.32), indicating widespread maintenance failures in a district with many older mid-rise residential and mixed-use buildings.
evidence: 15 elevator complaints last week vs. 4.4 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
243% spike affects mobility for elderly, disabled, and families with strollers in older building stock (Borough Park has many 6-12 story pre-war residential buildings)
reporting_angles: Building-by-building investigation: Which properties are repeat offenders? Are landlords ignoring DOB violations or facing contractor shortages?
DOB enforcement: Has the district requested more building inspectors (per recurring CB budget request)? Are violation/penalty cycles moving fast enough?
Resident impact: Profile families trapped in walkups or elderly tenants unable to leave homes; tie to broader housing maintenance/landlord accountability issues.

themes_detail.label: Encampment Reports Spike 700%
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 4 this week, up 700% from a 0.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 4.95), marking a sharp rise in visible homelessness or street sleeping in public spaces across Borough Park/Kensington.
evidence: 4 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.5 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
700% spike coincides with colder weather (seasonal pattern risk, but still statistically notable)
reporting_angles: Ground reporting: Photograph and map encampment locations (parks, transit stations, commercial districts). Interview unhoused individuals about triggers: housing shortage, shelter capacity, services availability.
City response: What are DHS outreach efforts in the district? Are shelter beds full? Any recent policy changes affecting placement?
Community tension: Talk to business owners and residents about perceptions of safety, sanitation, and service disruption; balance with dignity/rights framing.

themes_detail.label: Overgrown Trees Trimming Backlog
themes_detail.summary: Overgrown tree/branch complaints jumped to 7 last week, up 367% from a 1.5-per-week baseline over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 6.35), suggesting Parks or contractors are falling behind on street tree maintenance across the district.
evidence: 7 overgrown tree complaints last week vs. 1.5 per-week average over prior 8 weeks
367% spike suggests seasonal cycle (fall/winter growth) or contractor delay, not random variation
reporting_angles: Parks budget/staffing: Has NYC Parks' tree maintenance contract been delayed or understaffed? Request service request response times and completion rates.
Safety hazard: Document trees blocking street lights, obscuring traffic signals (ties to 377 traffic signal complaints in district), or creating pedestrian hazards.
Comparison: Check if this spike appears in other Brooklyn districts (seasonal pattern) or is unique to Community Board 312 (resource allocation issue).
